channel.title: The Awesome Ledger — awesome-claude-code
channel.description: New entries across the GitHub awesome ecosystem, diffed nightly.

item.title: i18next-localization — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by i18next - Agent Skill that takes an app from hardcoded strings to a localized one with i18next: stack detection, config, AST-based wrapping of strings in t(), key extraction, sync to Locize and AI translation. It regenerates the step-by-step prompt from the installed i18next-cli, so it cannot drift from the CLI.

item.title: geoai-skills — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by muend - Skills for geospatial analysis that require coordinate-system, spatial-validation and comparability checks before a result is reported, and narrow or refuse a claim the data cannot support. Ships a paired evaluation against a skills-disabled control arm.

item.title: pstack-claude — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Michael Denyer - Claude Code version of Lauren Tan's Poteto's pstack. Rigorous agent workflows with Cursor primitives translated to other agents. Supports multiple providers.

item.title: mcu-skills — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Alex New - A collection of board-specific Claude Code skills for microcontrollers firmware development, one per board, covering STM32, ESP32, ESP8266, RP2040/RP2350, nRF52840 and AVR.Each skill documents pin mapping, clock and peripheral pitfalls, PlatformIO/toolchain setup and flashing.

item.title: funes — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by David Corvoysier - Durable cross-agent memory for Claude Code, Codex, pi, and Hermes. Your memory is a Hugging Face dataset you own: recall it from any machine or share it with your team. Single binary, local index, pinned local embedding models.

item.title: Mycelium — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Håvard Bartnes - A plugin that holds the agent back from writing code until the builder has answered four questions in the repo: what the problem is, who has it, what is assumed, and what would show it to be wrong. The answers live in the repo as YAML the agent is held to, next to a decision log.

item.title: LinkedIn Skills — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Serge Bulaev - A set of skills for LinkedIn marketing: drafting posts, comments and replies, extracting the hook formula from a viral post, planning a week of content, rewriting a profile, and segmenting the people who engaged. Posts are read through Apify and published through Publora, and every skill shows a draft for approval before anything goes out.

item.title: Universal Exam Cram Coach — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by ZeKai Nie - A multimodal, grounded active-learning tutor engine for college textbooks. Mitigates AI hallucinations and diagram blindness with automated vector figure cropping, homework-solution auto-pairing, and cross-session persistent state. Benchmarked on STEM courseware to run on small models with significant token savings.

item.title: PLUR — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by plur-ai - Open, local-first engram memory for Claude Code. Engrams are plain-text YAML you can read, correct, and delete. The same memory is shared across MCP tools and multiple providers.

item.title: Agent Skills for Knowledge Work — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Hieu T. Luu - Skills for knowledge work rather than just coding, covering a variety of cognitive approaches to problem-solving: brainstorming, critical thinking, problem diagnosis, design thinking, market research, deep reading, Socratic tutoring, and more.

item.title: wattop — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Jasonm4130 - Terminal monitor for Apple Silicon Macs that shows live Claude Code and Codex sessions, including subagent and workflow trees, with output tokens/s, context fill and estimated cost beside CPU/GPU power, temperatures and fans. Reads local transcripts.

item.title: napkin-to-blueprint — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Tapas Mukherjee - A five-stage pipeline of Claude Code slash commands and specialized subagents that turns a raw product idea into a build-ready blueprint: an interview-driven brief, researched feature definitions, per-feature specs with acceptance criteria, and an architecture with a database schema.

item.title: mirrord — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by MetalBear - Agent skills and a Claude Code plugin marketplace for mirrord, which runs a local process inside a live Kubernetes cluster's network, environment and traffic. Lets Claude verify changes against real services, databases and queues instead of mocks, with skills for config, CI, database branching, Kafka queue splitting and preview environments.

item.title: geo-sleuth — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Oldcircle - An agent skill that geolocates a photo with no readable text. Single-purpose Python scripts search and rank candidates using OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view. The answer comes with a camera position, heading, error radius and an evidence image. NOTE: Scripts involve contact with Baidu and Yandex.

item.title: context-tax — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Harbor - A zero-dependency CLI (npx context-tax) that reads Claude Code session transcripts to measure what is sent on every turn before the first prompt: system prompt, MCP tool names, the skill listing and instruction files. It prices each item per use, counts skills sent without a description once the listing budget runs out, and context-tax fix points each finding at the setting that turns it off.

item.title: claude-carbon — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Gaëtan Wittebolle - Tracks the carbon footprint of Claude Code sessions, feautring a live CO2 estimate in the status line, computed locally from token usage, next to the session cost.

item.title: cc-semaphore — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by patakuti - A lightweight session monitor for parallel Claude Code sessions. Aggregates running/waiting/idle status across sessions into the OS status bar or system tray, with the same experience on native Linux (GNOME Shell extension) and Windows (system tray via WSL). Also includes a scriptable trigger system for state-transition commands.

item.title: bough — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by nickelsec - Reads Claude Code JSONL session transcripts and draws a project's history as a creatively-styled diagram: a day, the tasks inside it, and every prompt, with the ones that ended in a commit marked. Segments work from pauses in the record rather than anything the user labelled, and prompts can be searched by the words they contain.

item.title: bdg (Browser Debugger CLI) — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by szymdzum - A CLI and Claude Code skill for UI debugging in Chrome using the DevTools Protocol, including DOM inspection, browser events, rendered styles, and detailed layout information.

item.title: atelier — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Ethan Yucetepe - Claude Code plugin with eight design-automation skills driven by one schema-validated brand.json: design tokens for CSS, Tailwind, TypeScript and Figma, social cards, favicon and app-icon sets, responsive AVIF and WebP images, HTML-to-video recording, a WCAG 2.1 AA audit, and a runtime UX audit covering bfcache, INP, dialogs and mobile viewports.

item.title: Story Skills — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Daniel Dewhurst - Skills for planning and drafting fiction as markdown with YAML frontmatter: story bible, characters, worldbuilding, arcs, scenes, and chapters. Includes a dependency-free CLI whose continuity checker flags characters appearing after their death, payoffs placed before their setup, and stale story state.

item.title: Repowire — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Prassanna Ravishankar - A live mesh network that connects Claude Code and other providers so they can talk to each other in real time. Built for emergent coordination. Agents discover each other and share context across project boundaries. Uses tmux sessions as the coordination layer with logical "circles" for peer isolation. Includes a web dashboard and Telegram bot.

item.title: Pinpoint — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by gowtham012 - Local MCP server, Claude Code hooks and a Chrome extension for marking up a running app: clicking an element (or one in the iOS Simulator) and typing a change delivers the comment to Claude Code with the selector, DOM path, computed styles, component chain, source-file hint and a cropped screenshot.

item.title: OctoShell — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by savvasioakeim - Terminal workspace for Windows and macOS, built on command blocks, that runs Claude Code in git worktrees, one per task, each with its own shell and dev server. Features include Strategy Mode (several agents plan a change before writing code), a Reviewer agent that reads each change for regressions, and QA Mode (checklist over the running app).

item.title: Gryph — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by SafeDep - Gryph is a security layer for AI coding agents. It hooks into Claude Code and enforces YAML policy rules that block, warn, or guide actions in real time, then logs every event to a local SQLite database for review and audit.

item.title: Consort — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Kevin Hartman - Spec-first, test-driven agent framework: runs the build loop against live Lakebase Postgres branches under a deterministic orchestrator, with human-approval gates.

item.title: Codeburn — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by iamtoruk - Breakdown of local spend down by project, model, git branch and task. Tracks plan quotas, and identifies token waste, including unused MCP servers, verbose CLAUDE.md, repeated file reads, and more.

item.title: Claude Code Local — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Matt Macosko - Runs Claude Code fully on-device on Apple Silicon: a native MLX server speaks the Anthropic Messages API, so the unmodified claude CLI works against local Qwen, Gemma and Llama models with no cloud calls. Includes RAM-based model selection, a tool-call parser for local models' output formats, and a verified-offline mode.

item.title: Charrette — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Stefan Teofanovic - A Claude Code plugin with agent skills for designing software before code is written: brainstorm boards, plans cut into slices and run by subagents, working HTML mockups, development workbenches and layered pull request reviews. Every document renders live in a bundled local viewer with Mermaid diagrams, outside the repository.

item.title: Agents Can Communicate (ACC) — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Mykola Maksymenko - Local, multi-provider agent communication tool. Adds hooks and a skill to exchange questions and reviews, and saves decisions, verification results and handoffs for later sessions. Each session keeps its own client, model, conversation and permissions.

item.title: Agent 007 — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by bill10 - A self-hosted office with a pleasing pixel-art UI where one manager agent, Billion, takes a mission, posts jobs to a board, and reviews and merges pull requests that Claude Code and Codex workers open from their own git worktrees. Accessible from desktop or mobile.

item.title: clausona — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by larcane97 - A CLI and TUI for running several Claude Code accounts on one machine. Each account gets its own config directory through a shell hook, keeping its own sign-in and history, while plugins, settings, skills, commands and agents are symlinked to one primary directory.

item.title: OpenRig — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Mike Schwarz - Combines Claude Code, Codex, and Pi terminal sessions into persistent long-running teams. Agents message each other directly over tmux and queue work to each other, instead of the user relaying messages. Teams and agents are saved as YAML files, and a running team can be snapshotted and restored later.

item.title: Logo Designer Skill — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by neonwatty - Create and evolve SVG logos with Claude Code. Turns a project brief into distinct concepts you can compare side by side, then guides refinement, checks favicon legibility, and exports production-ready PNGs.

item.title: Archify — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by tt-a1i - An Agent Skill for Claude Code that generates interactive architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, and lifecycle diagrams as standalone HTML. Typed JSON, local renderers, and delivery checks support source-linked node details, path tracing, themes, and export.

item.title: vir — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Djordje Marković - Distills the Claude Code transcripts already on your disk into typed markdown notes (decisions, gotchas, patterns). Serves them via MCP and a CLAUDE.md block. Integrates with Obsidian.

item.title: ralph-harness — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Vitaly Kuprin - A CLI that runs Claude Code in a loop, with a fresh claude -p process for each iteration in a harness-owned git worktree.

item.title: oh-my-patent — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by illusionaireal - A plugin for turning technical ideas into patent disclosures.

item.title: localpr — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by gilles-g - Reviews Claude's uncommitted changes in a local GitHub-style pull request page: comment on any line, send comments in batches while Claude keeps working, ask Claude questions answered inline in the thread, and get each comment back marked fixed or refused.

item.title: learn-faster-kit — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Hugo Lau - A creative educational framework for Claude Code, inspired by the "FASTER" approach to self-teaching. Ships with a variety of agents, slash commands, and tools that enable Claude Code to help you progress at your own pace, employing well-established pedagogical techniques like active learning and spaced repetition.

item.title: claude-code-zsh-completion — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by 1160054 - Zsh completion for the Claude Code CLI. Dynamically completes sessions, MCP servers, agents, models and plugins from the user's configuration.

item.title: anotifier — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Amin Dhouib (Devino Solutions) - A zero-dependency, cross-platform notifier that fires a desktop toast and a free phone push (via ntfy) the moment Claude Code (or Codex/Cursor/Gemini) finishes a task or needs input, wired up by a one-command setup. The standout among notifiers is its testing rigor — CI drives the real agent CLIs end to end and asserts real ntfy round-trips and real OS toast delivery, no mocks.

item.title: Scientific Writing Skills — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by David Sosa-Trejo - Six Agent Skills for scientific writing based on Stanford's Writing in the Sciences course: sentence-level prose editing, IMRaD manuscript structure, the writing process, peer review and publication, grants and recommendation letters, and lay summaries and press. Ships as the sciwrite Claude Code plugin with four stdlib-only Python audit scripts.

item.title: SPARDA — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Zakaria Gharzouli (Residual Labs) - Converts a running Express or FastAPI app into an MCP server by AST-parsing its routes and injecting a marked, byte-for-byte-removable /mcp router, so the agent can operate your live application (real auth, real data) rather than just read files. Exceptionally safety-minded: writes are disabled by default behind two-phase confirmation, docstrings are sanitized against prompt injection, a circuit-breaker quarantines failing routes, nothing leaves the machine, and persistence stores structure never payloads.

item.title: Cooklang skills — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by dubadub - Skills and an MCP server that let AI agents work with Cooklang recipes: plain-text .cook recipes and .menu meal plans in a folder you own.

item.title: Claude Scientific Skills — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by K-Dense - "A set of ready-to-use Agent Skills for research, science, engineering, analysis, finance and writing." That's their description - modest, simple. That's how you can tell this is really one of the best skills repos on GitHub. If you've ever thought about getting a PhD... just read all of these documents instead. Also I think it IS an AI agent or something? Awesome.

item.title: Claude CLI ↔ Telegram — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Imolatte - A feature-rich Telegram bot that turns your machine into a remote Claude Code terminal driven from your phone: streaming tool progress, voice input, a git panel, Mac remote control, and 30+ commands. Its standout is the approval flow — dangerous-op Approve/Deny taps are injected straight into the real terminal prompt via tmux send-keys, so you authorize from your phone without killing the session or losing context.

item.title: Awesome Claude Code Mods — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by Karan Bansal - A community list of Claude Code mods built with function hooks. Scans public GitHub repositories and shows what the validator reports each mod can read, write, run or send over the network.

item.title: Agent Workbench — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by cvelasquez - Local web UI that runs the unmodified Claude Code CLI in a pseudo-terminal and adds tabs, a browsable history of past sessions, conversations rendered as cards, a context meter, and the agent's multiple-choice questions answered from the UI.

item.title: pwa2play — via awesome-claude-code
item.description: by degordonstech - Packages a PWA into a signed Play Store Android bundle with Bubblewrap and checks target API level, signing key reuse, assetlinks fingerprints and version codes before upload.
